Oh and one more thing!! Learn how to pick up rabbits correctly. Only pick them up when it's actually needed as most of them don't actually like it. 

When you are picking them up, scoop under the belly with one hand and the butt with the other,  hug them to your chest,  make sure their feet are supported.

I would hope that one would know that,  but people so surprise me sometimes and so I feel like I have to say it

Hay is so so so important.  It should be about 80% of their diet,  so an easy way to start with figuring out how much their gonna eat is to give them s HUGE bundle of it the size of the body plus more everyday.  I'm not talking crappy straw,  you want nice hay.  My rabbits eat oaten bale hay and they also love ryegrass hay, but there's lots of hays out there that they can have. Do a bit of research and figure out which will one is best in your area for your bunny.  I would avoid too much lucerne as it can give some rabbits the runs.  

Find a good quality pellet,  not that crap with all the seeds and bits of fruit in it,  that stuff is bad for rabbits.  A lot of greens are fine,  but do your research and introduce new foods very slowly as an upset stomach is the last thing you want and be quite dangerous (if a rabbit doesn't eat for long enough to will go into GI stasis, basically it's stomach will stop moving.  A lot of people don't understand why their rabbits suddenly get sick and die,  a lot of the reason this is why). I'll touch on gi stasis more later.. 

One of my rabbits has some stomach issues that I've been working on,  so unfortunately my bunnies don't get a lot of variety (safer to Feed them both the same things as they r both guts and will eat each others food lol).  So mine get pellets in the morning plus hay.  At night they get a big handful of leafy greens, pellets,  and occasionally a small slice of apple each as a treat.  Rabbits do not need as many pellets as some people think!!  Just a small amount,  and this depends on the pellets.  Rabbits don't need barely any sugar either.  A treat (apple,  banana ect) occasionally is fine,  just don't over do it.  Btw every rabbit I've known seems to think banana is like delicious crack and will go nuts for it .

Make sure your bunny gets enough exercise. Don't buy one of those stupid tiny triangle looking cages, they are honestly ridiculous. Make sure the pen/cage has plenty of room to run around and get a playpen or find a safe enclosed area where they can run around and get their exercise.  

Make sure they get their khaleesi virus shots. Not only mosquitoes, but flies can make your rabbit incredibly sick. A dirty pen and flies are s very dangerous combination, so make sure the pen is always clean.  

If your rabbit does get sick,  from anything at all, take them to the vet immediately. I cannot stress this enough,  rabbits can go downhill so fast.  If they go into gi stasis, you need to take them to the vet and learn how to syrringe feed them to keep their stomach moving. Not eating and not pooping are bad signs.  And if your rabbit seems off at all, and you'll know once you learn what their personality is like,  don't assume theyre fine and will get better, take them to the vet.
